Elliot — thanks for the summary. Quick thoughts from a commercial ops perspective:

1) Channel treatment: For a 6% consignment margin we usually recommend a holdback with a quarterly true-up. That gives us a clean audit trail and avoids manual pass-throughs on every invoice. It does mean Redwood recognizes revenue net of the reserve until the true-up is settled.
2) Promo credit: If the credit is time-limited and applies to net spend, the cleanest is an invoice-level credit recorded as a contra-revenue line. Marketplace couponing is possible but AWS private offers impose constraints on how coupons display the post-credit amount — procurement wants to see the effective price in their dashboard which complicates things.
3) SKU packaging: Keep the same SKU but add a 'promo' line item for the first 3 invoices. Alternatively, create a 3-month SKU bundle that collapses into the standard SKU after month 3. The bundle approach gives a simpler amortization path for finance.

I'll add examples in the consignment_margin_table.xlsx showing holdback vs pass-through P&L impact. If Laura agrees, I think holdback + invoice credit matches our standard processes.

- Ben

Katie — thanks, noted. Attached: promo_credit_onepager.docx and an updated consignment_margin_table.xlsx that shows both workflows (direct remit vs Redwood holdback) with example journal entries. Quick answers inline then a recommended approach.

- Remit vs holdback: We recommend Redwood books the revenue and holds a 6% reserve, remitting to MedEquip on a quarterly basis after usage verification. This keeps the private offer clean in the marketplace UI (list price unchanged) while enabling auditability.
- Net-of-credit visibility: AWS does not currently show a post-credit net price in the private offer landing screen. You can see invoice-level credits in billing exports. To meet your procurement ask, we'll provide a standardized invoice artifact (PDF) and a one-line summary that shows effective monthly price in the offer email and in our billing documents.
- Packaging: I recommend a 3-month "promo bundle" SKU that lists at the same per-seat rate but carries a contra-revenue promo line that amortizes over three months. The bundle can be configured to collapse automatically to the standard SKU after month 3. See the attached table for amortization schedules.

Next steps:
1) Ben/Laura/Irene to confirm accounting path (holdback vs pass-through) by Wednesday EOD.
2) If holdback is OK, we'll publish the private offer draft (private_offer_draft.pdf) to AWS and share the DocuSign link for Ava to accept.
3) I'll deliver the one-pager to Katie and MedEquip legal today.
